raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Sampling softmax currently enables FlashInfer's Cake kernel on SM103 but falls back to `torch.softmax` on SM100. FlashInfer 0.7.1 supports Cake on both. This change enables the existing fast path on SM100 without changing its dtype or shape limits.

## Modifications

Extend the runtime and registry gates to SM100 and update the kernel documentation. This also affects non-deterministic sampling in the regular sampler; deterministic sampling keeps `torch.softmax`.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU routing and registry checks and scoped formatting pass on the updated branch. Earlier B200 checks with FlashInfer 0.7.1 compared Cake with Torch and a float64 reference; maximum absolute error was 6.0e-7 against Torch and 2.3e-6 against float64, with finite normalized outputs and the same argmax. GLM-5.3-Flash decode/prefill comparisons had mean absolute log-prob differences of 0.0225 to 0.0242 with Cake and 0.0218 to 0.0234 on main; argmax agreement was 0.980 to 0.984 for both arms. These results were within baseline variation. Those GPU checks used a nightly overlay and predate the latest base update. The regular sampler has not been measured separately on SM100.

Run the CPU kernel namespace suites with `python -m pytest` and GPU sampling suites through the registered CI runner.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The server comparison used GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 with EAGLE 4/1/5 on TP4 B200. The branch files were overlaid on nightly commit 7224fce1b5e4, before the latest base update. No server run of the updated branch is available. Time per verify step:

| Streams | Main | Cake enabled | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 8.413 ms | 8.231 ms | 182 us (2.2%) |
| 4 | 12.119 ms | 11.936 ms | 183 us (1.5%) |
| 16 | 18.329 ms | 18.186 ms | 143 us (0.8%) |

This was a restart A/B comparison. At 16 streams, the observed change was only a few times larger than server-to-server variation. The 80-row verify call remains on Torch because the current gate supports at most 64 rows; the 16-stream result comes from other Cake call sites. TP8, other GPUs, non-speculative workloads and the regular sampler on SM100 remain unvalidated.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -5,6 +5,8 @@
 import subprocess
 import sys
 from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
 
 import pytest
 
@@ -14,6 +16,7 @@
 from sglang.kernels import KernelBackend, PlatformInfo
 from sglang.kernels.spec import CapabilityRequirement as Cap
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
 register_cpu_ci(est_time=24, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
 
@@ -127,6 +130,101 @@ def test_capabilities_or_semantics():
     assert K.capabilities_satisfied(Cap.CUDA, _SM90)  # single tolerated
 
 
+class TestCakeSoftmaxCapability(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        from sglang.kernels.cake_kernels import sampling as cake_sampling
+
+        self.cake_sampling = cake_sampling
+        self.cake_sampling._device_supported.cache_clear()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        self.cake_sampling._device_supported.cache_clear()
+        super().tearDown()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _logits(shape, dtype):
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            is_cuda=True,
+            dtype=dtype,
+            ndim=len(shape),
+            shape=shape,
+            is_contiguous=lambda: True,
+            device=SimpleNamespace(index=0),
+        )
+
+    def test_sampling_softmax_uses_cake_for_qualified_sm100_inputs(self):
+        import torch
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops import sampling as sampling_ops
+
+        logits = self._logits((1, 131072), torch.float32)
+        cake_result = object()
+        fallback_result = object()
+        with (
+            patch("torch.cuda.get_device_capability", return_value=(10, 0)),
+            patch.object(self.cake_sampling, "find_spec", return_value=object()),
+            patch.object(torch.version, "cuda", "13.0"),
+            patch.object(sampling_ops, "cake_softmax", return_value=cake_result),
+            patch.object(torch, "softmax", return_value=fallback_result) as fallback,
+        ):
+            result = sampling_ops.softmax(logits)
+
+        self.assertIs(result, cake_result)
+        fallback.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_sampling_softmax_falls_back_outside_qualified_domain(self):
+        import torch
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops import sampling as sampling_ops
+
+        for arch, shape in (
+            ((10, 2), (1, 131072)),
+            ((10, 0), (65, 131072)),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(arch=arch, shape=shape):
+                self.cake_sampling._device_supported.cache_clear()
+                logits = self._logits(shape, torch.float32)
+                cake_result = object()
+                fallback_result = object()
+                with (
+                    patch("torch.cuda.get_device_capability", return_value=arch),
+                    patch.object(
+                        self.cake_sampling, "find_spec", return_value=object()
+                    ),
+                    patch.object(torch.version, "cuda", "13.0"),
+                    patch.object(
+                        sampling_ops, "cake_softmax", return_value=cake_result
+                    ) as cake,
+                    patch.object(
+                        torch, "softmax", return_value=fallback_result
+                    ) as fallback,
+                ):
+                    result = sampling_ops.softmax(logits)
+
+                self.assertIs(result, fallback_result)
+                cake.assert_not_called()
+                fallback.assert_called_once_with(logits, dim=-1)
+
+    def test_sampling_softmax_registry_matches_supported_architectures(self):
+        spec = K.select_kernel("sampling.softmax", backend=KernelBackend.FLASHINFER)
+        supported = ((10, 0), (10, 3))
+        unsupported = ((9, 0), (10, 1), (10, 2), (12, 0))
+
+        for arch in supported:
+            platform = PlatformInfo(
+                device_type="cuda", cuda_arch_major=arch[0], cuda_arch_minor=arch[1]
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(spec.is_available(platform), arch)
+        for arch in unsupported:
+            platform = PlatformInfo(
+                device_type="cuda", cuda_arch_major=arch[0], cuda_arch_minor=arch[1]
+            )
+            self.assertFalse(spec.is_available(platform), arch)
+        self.assertFalse(spec.is_available(_CPU))
+        self.assertFalse(spec.is_available(_HIP))
+
